description.text:
The Pokémon Stamp Box (ポケモン切手BOX～ポケモンカードゲーム 見返り美人・月に雁セット～) was a Japan Post product released on 25 August 2021, in the 150th year of Japan's postal service and on the opening day of the Japan International Stamp Exhibition 2021 in Yokohama. A box printed like a Poké Ball held a sheet of ten stamps, three die-cut postcards of Pikachu, Eevee and Charizard, an Anytime Anywhere Family Pokémon Card Game, and two promo cards painted by Mitsuhiro Arita, Pikachu 227/S-P and Cramorant 226/S-P.

Eight of the stamps are drawn as Pokémon cards, from the original Venusaur, Charizard and Blastoise to Scorbunny, Yamper, Skwovet, Zacian and Zamazenta. The other two, 120-yen stamps that match the promo cards, put Pikachu and Cramorant into Beauty Looking Back and Wild Geese Flying under the Full Moon, the pictures on the Philatelic Week stamps of 1948 and 1949, two of the most famous stamps Japan has issued.

Japan Post planned 80,000 boxes for its central post offices and online shop. On 21 July 2021, after a response beyond its expectations, it added 20,000 and sold every box by lottery instead: winners bought theirs at a post office, some not until late October, and 150 at the stamp exhibition. A second lottery for 7,000 boxes followed in February 2022, after some winners had not bought theirs.
